executiveComp.source: Advocate Health Inc FY2024 Form 990 Schedule J (EIN 88-4157429); Woods reported as Advocate Health CEO, not on CMHA filing. All 21 Atrium-level executives earned at least $1.49M. Former co-CEO James Skogsbergh received $28.9M in FY2024. Woods' comp rose 49% from $17.25M in FY2023.

communityBenefit.source: Atrium Health claimed $2.38B community benefit across NC in 2025 (Atrium Health newsroom, July 2026). NC nonprofit hospital charity care state average of 2.4% of operating budgets per Lown Institute 2024 state report. 85% of NC nonprofit hospitals had fair share deficits per Lown analysis. Atrium-specific charity care as pct of revenue not separately verified.

taxAdvantage.notes: CMHA is a unit of local government (Charlotte-Mecklenburg Hospital Authority) with automatic exemptions from property tax, income tax, sales tax, and motor fuel tax, plus power of eminent domain. Mecklenburg County assessed Atrium property at $1.72B; Atrium and Novant combined avoided $23M in property taxes in that county alone (2022). Atrium reported $252M in 340B savings in 2020 ($693M cumulative 2018-2020). Bond debt of $3.1B generates significant tax-exempt interest subsidy.

keyRiskFactors: Carries strongest credit rating among top five largest US health systems
Merger integration achieving nearly $1.1B in annual synergies
Strong balance-sheet metrics and leading market positions across multiple states
Exposure to North Carolina State Health Plan reimbursement disputes
